children.label: c
children.prompt: Find the coordinates of any points of inflection.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}-6(x-1)&=0\\x&=1.\\y(1)&=-1+3+9-27\\&=-16.\end{align*}$$
For $x<1$, $y''>0$; for $x>1$, $y''<0$. The concavity changes from up to down, so $(1,-16)$ is a point of inflection.

children.prompt: Sketch the graph of the function, indicating all important features.

answer.short: Cubic with local minimum $(-1,-32)$, local maximum $(3,0)$, inflection point $(1,-16)$, $y$-intercept $(0,-27)$ and $x$-intercepts $(-3,0)$ and $(3,0)$. The curve falls from the upper left to the lower right.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}y&=-x^3+3x^2+9x-27\\&=-x^2(x-3)+9(x-3)\\&=(x-3)(9-x^2)\\&=-(x-3)^2(x+3).\end{align*}$$
For the $x$-intercepts:
$$\begin{align*}-(x-3)^2(x+3)&=0\\x&=3\text{ or }-3.\end{align*}$$
At $x=0$, $y=-27$. The curve decreases for $x<-1$, increases for $-1<x<3$, and decreases for $x>3$, touching the $x$-axis at its maximum $(3,0)$. It is concave up for $x<1$ and concave down for $x>1$. As $x\to-\infty$, $y\to\infty$; as $x\to\infty$, $y\to-\infty$. Draw a smooth cubic through the intercepts, stationary points and inflection point.
